reason: Both push back, cap liability, narrow the IP indemnity and allow conceding uncapped IP indemnity. B is stronger. It states the cap at 12 months of fees with a fallback, lists the standard uncapped carve-outs, and names the key asymmetry as the walk-away line: uncapped general liability could bankrupt the company. It also explains that the C-corp protects personal assets, and it adds useful tactics (one redline pass, "insurer requires" framing, insurance-limit caps). A includes an odd, unsupported claim about losing IP in bankruptcy and an aggressive US-only IP scope. It also gives a $1M super-cap with little reasoning and has a slightly contradictory "hold firm" list. B's extra checklist items are somewhat broad, but they are useful and not mere padding.
